In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 73, verses 1–4:

(p-٥٩٥٧) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Muzzammil

al-Mahayimi said: It was named thus because it indicates the great weight of the matter of revelation, for the strongest of creatures would tremble in its presence and wrap himself up (yatazammalu).

It is Meccan. It is said: except His statement, Exalted is He, "Indeed your Lord knows..." to the end of the surah. Its verses number twenty.

(p-٥٩٥٨) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion on the interpretation of His statement, Exalted is He:

[1–4] ﴿O you who wrap yourself in garments!﴾ ﴿Stand [in prayer] by night, except for a little,﴾ ﴿half of it, or subtract from it a little,﴾ ﴿or add to it, and recite the Qur'an in measured recitation.﴾

﴿O you who wrap yourself in garments!﴾ That is, the one who wraps himself (al-mutazammil), from tazammala bi-thiyabihi, when he wraps himself in them. The ta' was assimilated into the za' (تزمّل → المزّمّل). He, may blessings and peace be upon him, was addressed by describing his state at the time the revelation descended, out of gentleness, reassurance, and encouragement to exert himself in standing for the night prayer. It is also said that its meaning is the one who bears the burdens of prophethood, from tazammala al-ziml, when one bears a heavy load. Thus there is a metaphor: the carrying out of the conveyance of the message is likened to bearing a heavy load, with the common factor being hardship.

Al-Shihab said: It has been objected that, even granting the validity of the literal meaning and its support by the authentic hadiths, there is no basis for claiming a figurative usage here.

It may be answered that the hadiths were related concerning the descent of the surah al-Muddaththir, not this surah, as will come, God willing, unless it is said that both have one meaning.

﴿Stand [in prayer] by night﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 2], that is, perform the prayer during it, and leave off wrapping oneself up for sleep. ﴿except for a little﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 2], that is, by necessity, for rest and the needs of the body, without which it cannot continue.

Then He, Exalted is He, specified the amount of standing in prayer, leaving the choice to him, saying:

﴿half of it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3], that is, half of the night, is a substitute (badal) for "the night."

﴿or subtract from it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3], that is, from the half, ﴿a little﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3], that is, down to a third.

﴿or add to it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 4], that is, the half up to two-thirds. The intent is to give choice between standing for half, more than that, or less than that. It is not asked how half can be "a little" when it equals the other half; for the littleness is relative to the whole, not to its counterpart.

(p-٥٩٥٩) ﴿and recite the Qur'an in measured recitation﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 4], that is, make it clear with clarity, and recite it slowly and deliberately.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Tartil of the Qur'an is reciting it with deliberation and calmness, making the letters distinct, prolonging the vowels, until what is recited from it resembles a well-arranged row of teeth (al-thaghr al-murattal), which is the one with gaps, likened to the light of the chamomile (al-uqhuwan); and that one should not hurry through it, nor pour it out in a rush.

Note:

Al-Suyuti said: The verse indicates the recommendation of reciting with tartil, and that it is better than reciting hastily. This is clear.

It is established in the Sunnah that he, may blessings and peace be upon him, "used to pause in his recitation verse by verse, and that it was clearly explained letter by letter, and that he would stop at the ends of the verses."

The verse has been used as evidence that tartil and reflection, with little recitation, are better than speed of recitation with much of it; for the purpose of the Qur'an is understanding it, reflecting upon it, comprehending it, and acting upon it.

Ibn Mas'ud said: Do not rush through the Qur'an as one rushes through poetry, nor scatter it as one scatters dates of poor quality. Stop at its wonders, move hearts with it, and let not the concern of any one of you be to reach the end of the surah.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[5] ﴿Indeed, We are going to send down upon you a heavy word.﴾

﴿Indeed, We are going to send down upon you a heavy word.﴾ That is: weighty (raṣīnan), owing to the solidity of its wording, the firmness of its meaning, and its superiority in both over everything else.

Since weightiness is the predominant characteristic of it, "heavy" (thaqīl) is used figuratively for this quality. Or [it means]: heavy upon the one who reflects on it, because it requires an increase in the purification of the inner self (sirr) and the stripping away of distraction from one's contemplation. Or [it means]: heavy to receive, based on the statement of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "I saw him ﷺ receiving revelation on a very cold day, and it would part from him, and his forehead would be dripping with sweat." Either way, the sentence gives the reason for the command to recite slowly and deliberately (tartīl), and that its weight is something that calls for it.

(p-5960)

Commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[6] [5] ﴿Indeed, the rising at night (nashi'at al-layl) is more potent in its effect and more upright in speech.﴾

﴿Indeed, the rising at night﴾, i.e., its beginning, its natural character and its manifest form. ﴿Is more potent in its effect﴾, i.e., more conducive to what is intended from it, namely the gathering of the heart and the calm of the mind.

﴿And more upright in speech﴾, i.e., more forceful in utterance and more correct.

Ibn Qutaybah said: Because at night voices become still, movements cease, speech becomes pure, and there is no barrier to hearing it and understanding it.

Al-Suyuti related from al-Jahiz, who said: "The rising at night" is the meanings derived from the Qur'an at night. "More potent in its effect" means its impression is clearer. "And more upright in speech" means it is more correct than what thoughts produce by day, because the hearing and the sight are free from preoccupation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 73, verses 7–9:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7–9] ﴿Indeed, for you by day is prolonged occupation.﴾ ﴿And mention the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with devotion.﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 8] ﴿Lord of the east and the west; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Trustee.﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 9]

﴿Indeed, for you by day is prolonged occupation﴾ means: a turning about in your affairs and being busied with them; therefore you were commanded to stand in prayer at night.

﴿And mention the name of your Lord﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 8] means: persist in remembering Him by night and by day. Al-Zamakhshari said: The remembrance of Allah encompasses everything that is good remembrance: glorification (tasbih), declaring His oneness (tahlil), magnifying (takbir), glorifying (tamjid), affirming His unity (tawhid), prayer (salah), recitation of the Qur'an, the study of knowledge, and other things with which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would fill the hours of his night and day.

﴿And devote yourself to Him with devotion﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 8] means: be sincere toward Him by stripping the self of other than Him, with great sincerity.

﴿Lord of the east and the west; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Trustee﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 9] means: entrust to Him your affairs, for He will suffice you in them.

Ibn Jarir said: That is, in what He commands you, and entrust to Him your means (asbab).

(p-5961)

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[10–14] ﴿And be patient over what they say, and part from them with a gracious parting.﴾ ﴿And leave Me with the deniers, the people of ease, and give them respite a little.﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 11] ﴿Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing fire.﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 12] ﴿And food that chokes, and a painful torment.﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 13] ﴿On the Day the earth and the mountains quake, and the mountains become a heap of scattered sand.﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 14]

﴿And be patient over what they say﴾, meaning: over the harm and the slander.

﴿And part from them with a gracious parting﴾, meaning: by turning away from repaying them in kind, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Heed not their harm, and put your trust in Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 48].

﴿And leave Me with the deniers﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 11], meaning: leave Me to deal with them and entrust their affair to Me, for I am sufficient for You in taking vengeance upon them.

﴿The people of ease﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 11], meaning: those of luxury (al-tan'um), referring to the chieftains (ṣanādīd) of Quraysh and their affluent ones (mutrafīhim).

﴿And give them respite a little﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 11], meaning: be patient with them for a time, or a brief respite.

﴿Indeed, with Us are shackles﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 12], meaning: chains (quyūd), the word being ankāl (shackles). ﴿And a blazing fire﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 12], meaning: a fire of intense heat and blaze. ﴿And food that chokes﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 13], meaning: one who eats it chokes on it and cannot swallow it. ﴿And a painful torment﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 13], meaning: another kind of torment, painful, whose true nature is not known. That is: you will not see those whose affair is left to Me being avenged upon in any way other than this vengeance.

﴿On the Day the earth and the mountains quake﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 14], meaning: they tremble and shake with the earthquake. ﴿And the mountains become a heap of scattered sand﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 14], meaning: loose sand, dispersed and scattered (kathīban mahīlan).

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[15–16] ﴿Indeed, We have sent to you a messenger, a witness over you, just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾ ﴿But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a severe seizing﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 16]

(p-5962) ﴿Indeed, We have sent to you a messenger, a witness over you﴾ i.e., by the acceptance of whoever accepted and the refusal of whoever refused. ﴿just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾ i.e., calling him to the truth.

﴿But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a severe seizing﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 16] i.e., heavy (wabil), and that by destroying him and those with him, drowning them in the sea (yamm).

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[17–19] ﴿How, then, will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, on a Day that will make the children grey-haired? The sky will be split asunder by it; His promise is ever to be fulfilled.﴾ ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.﴾

﴿How, then, will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, on a Day that will make the children grey-haired?﴾ That is: how will you protect yourselves if you remain in your disbelief and do not believe in the truth, on the Day of Resurrection, whose condition in terror is as has been mentioned.

Ibn Abi al-Hadid said: "The saying 'it makes the children grey-haired' in reference to a severe day is an expression that functions as a proverb (mathal). It is not literal, because the community is unanimous that children's features do not change to greyness in the Hereafter. The principle in this is that when worries and sorrows follow one another upon a person, he turns grey quickly." Abu al-Tayyib said:

"Worry wears down the large-framed through thinness, and it greys the forelock of the child and makes him aged."

﴿The sky will be split asunder by it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 18]. Al-Zamakhshari said: this is also a description of the day's severity, and that the sky, despite its greatness and firmness, will be split asunder in it, so what is your assumption about other creatures?

Al-Samin said: The attribute was not made feminine for one of these reasons:

Among them: it is interpreted as a derived noun (mushtaqq). Among them: it is of the form of relative adjective (nisba), meaning "possessing splitting," like "nursing (mudrii)" and "menstruating (ha'id)."

Among them: it may be used as both masculine and feminine. (p-5963) Among them: it is a collective noun (ism jins) distinguished from its single unit by the feminine ending, so one says "sama'a" (a single piece of sky), and collective nouns may take both masculine and feminine forms.

The bā' in "bihi" is causal (sababiyya), or instrumental (li-l-isti'ana), or in the sense of "fi" (in).

﴿His promise is ever to be fulfilled﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 18]. That is: because He does not break His promise, so beware of that Day.

﴿Indeed, this is﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 19], that is, the verses that speak of the severe threat, ﴿a reminder﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 19], that is, an admonition for whoever takes heed from them and is warned, ﴿so whoever wills may take a path to his Lord﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 19], that is, by believing in Him and acting in obedience to Him.

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) a little less than two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and so too a group of those with you. And Allah measures the night and the day. He knows that you cannot keep count of it, so He has turned to you (in forgiveness). So recite what is easy of the Qur'an. He knows that there will be among you those who are sick, and others who travel through the land seeking of Allah's bounty, and others who fight in the way of Allah. So recite what is easy of it, establish the prayer, give the zakat, lend to Allah a goodly loan. Whatever good you send forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah, better and greater in reward. And seek Allah's forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) a little less than two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it﴾ i.e., you perform the tahajjud in it at these various measures, and you exert yourselves in worship during it to this degree, in compliance with His command and devoting yourselves to Him. ﴿And a group of those with you﴾ i.e., He knows them to do likewise. ﴿And Allah measures the night and the day﴾ i.e., He has set them at measures by which they run, so that at times they are equal, and at times one of them increases at the expense of the other, and vice versa, which makes it difficult to persist in standing in prayer at night as He knows you would do. Ibn Kathir indicated this. Or the meaning is: the surah is of giving options, as a concession and facilitation.

﴿He knows that you cannot keep count of it﴾ i.e., standing in the night in the manner you were accustomed to, or standing the whole night, out of hardship and difficulty. ﴿So He has turned to you﴾ i.e., He returned to you with ease and the lifting of hardship.

﴿So recite what is easy of the Qur'an﴾ i.e., in the night prayer, without fixed measure. Or the intended meaning: do not exceed what He has determined for you, out of mercy toward yourselves. In it is a refutation of their excess in standing the whole night, or their eagerness for it, out of longing for worship and racing toward perfections.

Muqatil said: "A man would pray the whole night, fearing that he would not attain what he was commanded of the standing that was obligated upon him." (Transmitted by al-Razi.)

﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are sick﴾ i.e., sickness weakens them from standing in the night. ﴿And others who travel through the land﴾ i.e., for trade and other purposes, so that this keeps them from standing in the night. ﴿And others who fight in the way of Allah﴾ i.e., to support the religion, so they have no leisure for standing in it. ﴿So recite what is easy of it﴾ i.e., of the Qur'an, and do not burden yourselves; for He, exalted is He, intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you.

Remarks:

First: Many of the early scholars held that the standing in the night understood from the command to it at the beginning of the surah was obligatory, and it was abrogated by these verses.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Aisha, who said: "I used to place a mat for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to pray upon at night. People heard of it and gathered, and he came out as one angered — and he was merciful toward them — and he feared that the night prayer would be prescribed upon them. He said: 'O people! Take on of the deeds what you are able to do, for Allah does not tire of rewarding until you tire of doing, and the best of deeds is that which you persist in.'" And the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿O you who wrap yourself (in garments)﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 1] ﴿Stand (in prayer) through the night, except a little﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 2], and so on, until a man would tie a rope and hang on to it. They remained at this for eight months. Then Allah saw what they sought of His pleasure, had mercy on them, returned them to the obligatory prayer, and abandoned the obligation of the night standing.

Ibn Kathir said: The hadith in the "Sahih" is without the addition of the revelation of this surah, and this context may give the impression that this surah was revealed at Medina, but this is not so; rather it is Meccan. End of his words.

(p-5965) I say: By a narration like this it is inferred that the intent of the early scholars in saying "the verse was revealed" is the citing of it in a matter to which it applies, as we have explained many times.

It was also related from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah commanded His Prophet and the believers to stand in the night except a little, and this was hard upon the believers. Then He lightened it for them, having mercy on them, and Allah revealed after this: ﴿He knows that there will be among you﴾ — the verse. So Allah widened it, and to Him be praise, and did not constrict it.

And from Abu Abd al-Rahman, who said: When ﴿O you who wrap yourself﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 1] was revealed, they performed it for a year until their feet and shins swelled, until ﴿So recite what is easy of it﴾ was revealed, and the people rested.

Likewise it was narrated from Sa'id, al-Hasan, Ikrimah and Qatadah.

Ibn Hajar said in his "Sharh al-Bukhari": Some held that the night prayer was obligatory, then abrogated by standing for part of the night in general, then abrogated by the five prayers. al-Marwazi rejected this. And some held that before the Night Journey there was no obligatory prayer.

al-Suyuti said in "al-Iklil": His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Stand (in prayer) through the night, except a little﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 2] is abrogated after having been obligatory, by the end of the surah. It was said: it is muhkam (not abrogated), and so it was used as evidence for the recommendation of night standing. A group used it as evidence for its obligation upon the Prophet ﷺ specifically. Others for its obligation upon the community too, but not the whole night, rather the prayer of part of it; this is the view of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin. End of his words.

I say: Whoever holds that the command is muhkam and that it is for recommendation sees that the end of the surah is a teaching for them of kindness toward themselves, since He turned to them with ease and lifted from them the burdens. In it is what indicates their care for the recommended act and their eagerness for it, to the point that the situation came to kindness toward them in it. Aisha's report about their tying the rope to hang on to it, seeking aid in reciting the Qur'an and increasing its recitation, also indicates this.

Second: Ibn Kathir said: In His saying, exalted is He:

﴿So recite what is easy of the Qur'an﴾ is an expression for (p-5966) the prayer by recitation, as He said in the surah of Subhan: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾ [al-Isra: 110], i.e., in your recitation. The companions of Imam Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, used this verse as evidence that the recitation of al-Fatiha is not specified in prayer; rather, if one recites it or something else of the Qur'an, even a single verse, it suffices. They reinforced this with the hadith of the one who prayed badly, which is in the "Two Sahihs": "Then recite what is easy with you of the Qur'an." The majority answered them with the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, also in the "Two Sahihs," that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no prayer except for one who recites the Opening of the Book." End of his words.

Third: In His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And others who fight in the way of Allah﴾ is one of the signs of prophethood.

Ibn Kathir said: This verse, indeed the whole surah, is Meccan. Fighting had not yet been legislated, so it is among the greatest proofs of prophethood, since it is of the category of reporting unseen future matters.

Fourth: Ibn al-Faras said: In His saying:

﴿And others who travel through the land seeking of Allah's bounty﴾ is the virtue of trade, since it is placed in the verse alongside jihad.

Sa'id ibn Mansur related from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: "There is no state in which death comes to me, after jihad in the way of Allah, more beloved to me than that it come to me while I am seeking of Allah's bounty." Then he recited this verse.

al-Suyuti said: This verse is a basis for trade.

(p-5967) ﴿And establish the prayer and give the zakat﴾ i.e., the zakat of your wealth.

Ibn Kathir said: This indicates that whoever holds that the obligation of zakat was revealed at Mecca is supported, but the measures of the minimum thresholds and the amount to be paid were not specified until Medina.

﴿And lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾ means by it spending wealth in the way of good deeds in the best manner, being of the best of one's wealth, giving it to the deserving without delay, and guarding against reminders and harm. The secret of the command with "goodly" is that a loan is given with the intention of receiving it back, so one does not mind what or how much is given from it; hence attention is drawn to preferring the higher station. And because its return to the lender is certain, the expression with it indicates the certainty of the recompense here.

﴿Whatever good you send forward for yourselves﴾ i.e., in this world, of charity or expenditure in the ways of good, or deeds of obedience to Allah, or other acts of righteousness, ﴿you will find it with Allah, better and greater in reward﴾ i.e., in reward, than what you have of the enjoyments of this world.

﴿And seek Allah's forgiveness﴾ i.e., ask Him to forgive your sins. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ i.e., possessor of forgiveness for the sins of whoever turns to Him and repents, and mercy in not punishing you for them after their repentance from them.
